citedUrls.notes: Opened by zackees on Sep 18, 2026. Repo page shows Star 0 / Fork 0. Issue header shows 'Closed #33' - already resolved in-repo. Both cited quotes present verbatim: 'Bar length proportional to time is the honest encoding, and it is the only way to show "how long does a link take".' (decision D4) and 'The README and https://zackees.github.io/llvm-ld/ show two line charts that answer the wrong question.' / 'Nobody needs the history; we care about current performance.' Reads as a machine-drafted design-review spec (a D1-D9 decision table with rationales), not a demand posted to an audience. D5 asks for an interquartile-range whisker on every bar; D6 asks for light and dark variants; D7 asks for direct-labelled bars because a hotlinked SVG has no hover layer.

newSources.why: hyperfine, Star 28.9k / Fork 510, ships SIX matplotlib plotting scripts - plot_benchmark_comparison.py, plot_whisker.py, plot_histogram.py, plot_parametrized.py, plot_progression.py, advanced_statistics.py, welch_ttest.py. README verbatim: 'This folder contains scripts that can be used in combination with hyperfines --export-json option.' and 'To make these scripts work, you will need numpy , matplotlib and scipy .' Verbatim: 'there's just far too much for a human to absorb, all presented at once', 'Overall text size is quite small, and difficult to read', 'A significant proportion of the free text is caveats. Direct support for a hard row cap, a large type floor, and a single one-line caveat rather than a caveat paragraph. news.ycombinator.com returned HTTP 429; read via the Algolia item API.

collinfunk on the 'Rewriting in Rust' thread. Verbatim: 'Note, I am a co-maintainer of GNU coreutils.' / 'I really wished the documented their benchmarking methodology here, or at least cautioned the reader not to jump to conclusions based on the benchmarks shown.' / 'I find it a bit frustrating that benchmarks are thrown out without any methodology or citations, because they are often trusted without question.' Confirms the candidate's risk #6 - a chart without conditions is a footgun.

CONTRADICTS the candidate's 'almost none of them carry a chart'. Lemire ships five chart images AND matching numeric tables in one post (Geekbench single/multi-core, base vs max boost frequency, transistor counts, cache/dispatch/ALU/reorder-buffer, SIMD units). Reframes the need: the want is proven, and the per-post workload is five charts, not one.

The #1 perf post on HN that week - 'We made Playwright 2x faster and 80% more token efficient', 150 points, 2026-09-18, item 49756671 - points here. The README carries only the plain-text line 'Point the same script at Browserbase and get 2x faster execution than Playwright cloud equivalent browsers.' No chart, no table, no numbers at all. The purest instance of the gap.

Volume check on the candidate's 'several a week' claim. The 2026-09-18..21 window alone returns ~10 perf-claim submissions: 'We made Playwright 2x faster and 80% more token efficient' (150), 'How did AMD Ryzen get 50% faster in two years?' (71), 'I built the fastest PHP webserver in the world' (44), 'How did Apple Silicon get 50% faster in three years?' (26), 'Qbix Server - PHP 100x faster than Nginx and PHP-fpm', 'Faster JSON parsing with SVE2 on ARM processors', 'Splash Engine - The Fastest Local Qwen3.8 on Apple Silicon', 'Fastest Coding Agent (5x faster than Codex)'. The cadence claim holds.
